title: The rack
learned: A patch is a rack of modules; each module does one job
Knobs are on the front, sockets on the back: Tab turns the rack, F1 / F2 pick a side
The back is where you decide how sound and control voltages flow

steps.why: Every sound in PatchCore comes from small modules in a rack, the way hardware synths were built before everything fitted in one box. Each module does one job: makes a tone, filters it, sets the volume. The power comes from how you connect them.
steps.do: Look at the four modules in front of you: an oscillator (makes the tone), an amplifier (sets the volume), a scope (shows voltages) and a patchbay. Press Next.

steps.why: A rack soon gets wider than the window, so you need to move around it.
steps.do: Move around: drag with the middle mouse button, or turn the mouse wheel over an empty spot (up and down; Shift+wheel sideways), or use the arrow keys. Zoom with Ctrl+wheel over an empty spot. The Navigator on the right shows the whole rack and where you are. Press Next when you are comfortable.
steps.after: The rack never ends: you can always make room for one more module.

steps.why: JXMP modules keep their knobs on the front and their sockets on the back, like rack gear in a studio. The front stays clean for playing, the back is for wiring.
steps.do: Press Tab to turn the rack around.
steps.after: You see the back now: every round socket is an input or an output. Outputs send a voltage, inputs receive one. Nothing is wired yet, so nothing sounds.
steps.try: Hover a socket: the tooltip says what it carries.

steps.why: Tab always flips. When you want a known side, use F1 for the front and F2 for the back.
steps.do: Press F1 to come back to the front.
steps.after: Front for playing, back for patching. Most lessons will ask you to switch between them: the panel tells you which side a step needs.
steps.try: Press F2 and F1 a few times; the rack turns each time.

steps.why: Basic modules from other makers (and the Host Audio / Host MIDI modules that talk to your sound card and keyboard) have their sockets on the front. The patchbay is the bridge between the two sides.
steps.do: Find the patchbay (JX-PB4) in the rack. You will use it in a later lesson. Press Next to finish.
